arxiv-2212-11349.title: Lattice vibrational modes in changchengite from Raman spectroscopy and first principles electronic structure
arxiv-2212-11349.creator: B. Chatterjee, D. Vengust, A. Mrzel, P.Sutar, E. Goreshnik, J. Mravlje, T. Mertelj
arxiv-2212-11349.description: Abstract We measured room-temperature phonon Raman spectra of changchengite (IrBiS) and compared the experimental phonon wavenumbers to the theoretical ones obtained by means of the ab initio density-functional-theory calculations in the presence and absence of the spin-orbit coupling effects. Combining two different excitation photon energies all the symmetry predicted Raman modes are experimentally observed.

arxiv-2309-13122.title: The dominant mechanism(s) for populating the outskirts of star clusters with neutron star binaries The dominant mechanism(s) for populating the outskirts of star clusters with neutron star binaries – References 2011
arxiv-2309-13122.creator: Nathan W. C. Leigh, Claire S. Ye, Steffani M. Grondin, Giacomo Fragione, Jeremy J. Webb, Craig O. Heinke
arxiv-2309-13122.description: Abstract It has been argued that heavy binaries composed of neutron stars (NSs) and millisecond pulsars (MSPs) can end up in the outskirts of star clusters via an interaction with a massive black hole (BH) binary expelling them from the core. We argue here, however, that this mechanism will rarely account for such observed objects.

arxiv-2312-14189.description: Abstract Phase space reconstruction methods allow for the analysis of low-dimensional data with methods from dynamical system theory, but their application to prediction models, like those from machine learning, is limited. arxiv-2506-06936.title: A Combinatorial Approach to Novel Boundary Design in Deterministic Lateral Displacement

arxiv-2506-06936.description: Abstract Deterministic lateral displacement (DLD) is a high-resolution separation technique used in various fields. A fundamental challenge in DLD is ensuring uniform flow characteristics across channel, particularly near sidewalls where pillar matrix inevitably loses its lateral periodicity. Despite attempts in the literature to improve boundary design, significant variations in critical diameter persist near sidewalls, adversely affecting the separation performance.
